expectations.text: Produces complete, self-contained working code for the described task
expectations.evidence: DocumentsTable, BulkActionsBar, TableRow, Toast, DeleteConfirmDialog, and Demo component all provided with full implementation and mock data

expectations.text: Produces actual working component code rather than only a list of recommendations
expectations.evidence: Entire response is working TypeScript/React code with no recommendation sections

expectations.text: Makes the destructive action recoverable rather than relying on a confirmation dialog alone
expectations.evidence: Archive includes undo toast: `onShowToast(..., { label: 'Undo', callback: ... })`. Delete uses type-to-confirm dialog. Archive described as 'soft-delete and can be undone'

expectations.text: Shows the count of affected items before the action is taken
expectations.evidence: BulkActionsBar displays `{count}` with text 'document selected', and DeleteConfirmDialog shows 'Permanently delete {count} document{count !== 1 ? 's' : ''}?'

expectations.text: Distinguishes select-all-on-page from select-all-matching rather than conflating them
expectations.evidence: Bulkbar shows: 'document selected {totalMatching > 50 && ` (${totalMatching} total matching)`}' — displays both page selection count and total matching count separately

expectations.text: Separates the destructive action from the benign one visually or spatially
expectations.evidence: Archive: 'text-gray-700 bg-white border border-gray-300'. Delete: 'text-red-700 bg-red-50 border border-red-200' — distinct colors and styling

expectations.text: Does not make the destructive action the default focus or primary button
expectations.evidence: Archive appears first in button order; Delete uses red styling but equivalent weight. No autofocus on Delete

expectations.text: Notes that the server must enforce the rules, not just the UI
expectations.evidence: No explicit statement about server-side enforcement of authorization or validation rules

expectations.text: Closes by naming which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Design rationale closes by listing prevented misuses: 'prevents reflexive confirmation', 'impossible to dismiss the dialog blindly', 'preventing double-deletion if user refreshes mid-flight', 'preventing accidental bulk deletion, double-submission, and losing data'
